scope: CBSE Class 6 Social Science · Exploring Society: India and Beyond · Chapter 4 · Timeline and Sources of History
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 4 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion.

scenarios.need: Learner treats one surviving object or written clue as a complete and certain account of the past.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: single clue treated as complete proof rather than bounded evidence
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use fictional evidence cards to separate direct observations, cautious inferences and unanswered questions, without using personal family records or identity information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: For two unfamiliar evidence sets, independently distinguishes observation from inference and states at least one uncertainty that remains.

scenarios.need: Learner repeats a historical claim without identifying what evidence supports it or what additional evidence would test it.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: historical claim accepted without evidence trail or uncertainty check
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Match fictional claims to supporting clues, reject unsupported overclaims and identify one additional source that could strengthen or challenge each interpretation.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly classifies supported, unsupported and uncertain statements in two unfamiliar cases and proposes a relevant evidence check.

scenarios.need: Learner orders BCE dates by ordinary number size and therefore places a larger BCE year later instead of earlier.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: larger BCE number treated as later in time
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Order fictional BCE and CE date cards on a printed or cached timeline, then explain the BCE direction rule in simple language.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Orders an unfamiliar mixed BCE/CE set correctly and explains why larger BCE numbers are farther back in time.

scenarios.need: Learner confuses decade, century and millennium scales or estimates long historical intervals inconsistently.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: historical time scales confused or applied inconsistently
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Classify fictional time spans as decade-, century- or millennium-scale and compare intervals using only supplied dates.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly distinguishes 10-, 100- and 1,000-year scales and applies them to two unfamiliar timeline comparisons.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes a source is automatically reliable because it is old, written, official-looking or physical.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: source type or age treated as automatic proof of reliability
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional material, written and later descriptive sources by origin, purpose, limitation and what each can or cannot establish.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Evaluates two unfamiliar sources using at least two relevant reliability questions instead of accepting either source automatically.

scenarios.need: Learner treats disagreement between historical sources as proof that both sources are useless rather than evidence to investigate.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: source disagreement treated as automatic invalidation instead of corroboration task
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare three fictional accounts of the same event, identify agreement and disagreement, and state what additional evidence could corroborate competing claims.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains how conflicting sources can still be useful and identifies a sensible corroboration step in two unfamiliar cases.

scenarios.need: Learner turns limited evidence about early communities into certain claims about exact beliefs, ancestry, identity or migration routes.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: limited evidence overextended into certain claims about identity, ancestry, belief or migration
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use fictional settlement evidence to write one supported inference, one reasonable alternative and one remaining uncertainty, without asking for religion, caste, ancestry, genetics or family migration information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Produces cautious evidence-proportional interpretations for two unfamiliar early-community cases and clearly labels uncertainty.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a low-bandwidth, offline and instruction-light path for chronology and source reasoning that does not depend on cloud AI, live search, microphone, camera or personal-data collection.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, fictional source cards and local timeline prompts; complete one Kiki step at a time without live search, uploads, recordings or disclosure of family or identity information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes one evidence-and-change reasoning task plus mastery check using local resources only, with no personal data or remote service dependency.
